messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: HELP: Model identification for categorical exogenous variables
parts:
I think your problem comes down to this syntax:

#covariance of endogenous variables
trstMean~~disclosureScore

In your model, trstMean predicts disclosureScore. In regression, a predictor cannot have a free residual covariance with a its own dependent variable, unless there is a valid instrumental variable. In addition, your structural model is fully saturated (direct paths connect every pair of variables) without this residual covariance, so you have run out of information. Delete this residual covariance and I think your model will run.
Given that your two exogenous variables are randomized and thus truly exogenous, fixed.x = T is correct for your situation. If you want to be sure about what condition is being applied, put fixed.x = T into your call to the sem() function, after model and data.

On Thu, Jun 22, 2023 at 1:46 PM 'Lina Hillner' via lavaan <lav...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
Hi everyone,

I am currently trying to fit my first model using Lavaan in R and am new to SEM. 

My model (see picture attached) consists of two categorical exogenous variables (rapport, trustworthiness), one mediator (trust, continuous) and my outcome variable (disclosure, continuous). My exogenous variables were my experimental conditions with two levels each (present vs absent for each). Initially I thought I had 10 observations, and 8 parameters leaving me with df=2 but my code does not run and I am beginning to suspect that my model is underidentified. Let me know what you think.

Here are my questions/train of thoughts:
1. How does Lavaan determine model df for my model since my exogenous variables are categorical and do not yield any variance or covariance? 
Is Lavaan applying the fixed.x=T option, by default, and thus does not consider the exogenous variables when calculating the number of observations of the model? If so, that would leave me with only 3 observations and still 5 parameters making my model underidentified? 

Is there something I can do to still test my model? I assume I cannot simply act as if my categorical variables yield variance and covariances switching fixed.x=FALSE?

2. If I need to use the fixed.x option, where do I put it in the code? I get an error message when I put it in my model specification, my sem() function or my summary() function. Do I replace x with both my variable names? 

I did recode my exogenous variables as dummy variables with (0/1). But when I run the code, it shows me following error message:
Warning message:
In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING:
    Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could
    not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not
    identified.

Can you help me with any of these? I would really appreciate if anyone could point me in the right direction.
I'm not sure I understand all of this correctly as of yet. I just started reading on SEM and it is a little overwhelming. 

Thank you in advance for your help! 

Best wishes,
Lina

Here is my code. If you find any errors, do let me know:
#MODEL SPECIFICATION - Disclosure score 
model2 <- '
#Direct effects
disclosureScore ~ ctw*trustworthinessConditionRecoded + cr*interviewingConditionRecoded
#Mediator
trstMean ~ atw*trustworthinessConditionRecoded + ar*interviewingConditionRecoded
disclosureScore ~ b*trstMean
#Indirect effects
atwb := atw*b
arb := ar*b
#Total effects
totaltw := ctw + (atw*b)
totalr := cr + (ar*b)
#Variance of endogenous variables
trstMean~~trstMean
disclosureScore~~disclosureScore
#covariance of endogenous variables
trstMean~~disclosureScore
#intercepts
trstMean ~ 1
disclosureScore ~ 1'

fitmodel2 <- sem(model2, data = data)
fitmodel2
summary(fitmodel2, standardized = TRUE)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: HELP: Model identification for categorical exogenous variables
parts:
Lina--
     "fixed.x = T" does not hold anything constant. It says that your two exogenous variables are not subject to random sampling variance, because their values were *set* or chosen in your experiment design, not observed / sampled from some population. Therefore, the moments that only involve those variables--the variances of those predictors and their covariance--are also not subject to random sampling variance. That is why lavaan leaves those moments and those parameters (the variances of those predictors and their covariance) "out of the model." If those two variables really do not have random sampling variance, then treating them as if they did would be *overstating* the role of random sampling variance in your model.
     Yes, with no direct path from Trustworthiness to Disclosure, there should be 1 degree of freedom--that constraint is it. Your free parameters are:
4 regression paths
2 residual covariances (for the mediator and the outcome variable)
There are 7 moments available for estimating parameters in the covariance structure. starting with 10 (p = 4, p*(p+1)/2 = 10) but excluding the variances of the two predictors and their covariance, so 10 - 3 = 7. And 7 - 6 = 1 df.
     If you treated the predictors as sampled rather than selected (fixed.x = F), there would be 3 more moments to use in estimating parameters but also 3 more parameters to estimate, so degrees of freedom would be the same.
     I did not mention mean structure parameters (means or intercepts for the 4 variables) here because, in a single population model, the mean structure is typically saturated--4 mean structure parameters estimated using 4 sample means.

messages.subject: Re: HELP: Model identification for categorical exogenous variables
parts: lavaan's output should indicate the free parameters.  If you have 4 observed variables in your model, 8 free parameters and 1 degree of freedom, then it sounds like only 1 of your predictor variables is being treated as exogenous. Applying fixed.x=T to one of your two predictors would mean that you have 9 elements of the covariance matrix available, and could give you 8 free parameters. Obtaining that result, however, may involve an error in your syntax. The lavaan::summary() function or the lavaan::parameterEstimates() function will show you exactly which parameter estimates are free. In summary()< those are the parameter estimates that have estimated standard errors.

On Thursday, 22 June 2023 at 19:29:56 UTC+1 edward...@gmail.com wrote:
I think your problem comes down to this syntax:

#covariance of endogenous variables
trstMean~~disclosureScore

In your model, trstMean predicts disclosureScore. In regression, a predictor cannot have a free residual covariance with a its own dependent variable, unless there is a valid instrumental variable. In addition, your structural model is fully saturated (direct paths connect every pair of variables) without this residual covariance, so you have run out of information. Delete this residual covariance and I think your model will run.
Given that your two exogenous variables are randomized and thus truly exogenous, fixed.x = T is correct for your situation. If you want to be sure about what condition is being applied, put fixed.x = T into your call to the sem() function, after model and data.
